meaning:
ἀλαλάζω
(onomat. from the battle-cry ἀλαλά), [in LXX chiefly for רוּעַ hi., יָלַל ;]
prop, to raise a war-cry, shout with triumph or joy; rarely of grief, to wail: Mrk.5:38 (cf. Jer.4:8); of a cymbal, ἀλαλάζον (RV. clanging), 1Co.13:1 (cf. ὀλολύζω).†
(AS)

elsewhere.note: He came to the synagogue ruler’s house, and he saw an uproar, weeping, and great wailing.
If I speak with the languages of men and of angels, but don’t have love, I have become sounding brass, or a clanging cymbal.
